proposals.expected_failure_mode: If hospitalization timing varies within-season or differs from a fixed 2-week lag, forecasts may show phase error around the rise/peak.
proposals.rationale: Parsimonious seasonal template with waning immunity; a 2-week reporting/clinical lag from infections to hospitalizations matches the surveillance note while avoiding an explicit H compartment that may be weakly identifiable in a short series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-long lag can shift the predicted peak too late and smear the upswing, degrading short-horizon timing.
proposals.rationale: Same parsimony as SEIRS but allows a longer infection-to-admission lag, which can better align peaks when admissions are systematically later than incidence proxies.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H-related parameters may be weakly identifiable with 31 training weeks, leading to unstable attribution between I and H and overfitting of peak height/width.
proposals.rationale: Directly maps the target (hospitalization rate) to an explicit hospitalization compartment, capturing admission dynamics without relying on a fixed delay; suitable given high rate scale and moderate peakiness.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May blur mechanistic interpretation and inflate predicted levels if the model uses both I and H to explain the same signal, especially near the peak.
proposals.rationale: Robustifies observation by allowing the measured hospitalization signal to correlate with both infectious burden and hospitalized prevalence, which can help when admissions reflect a mixture of incident and prevalent severe cases.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If reinfection/waning immunity materially affects late-season dynamics, SEIR may underpredict rebounds or tail behavior.
proposals.rationale: Most parsimonious latent-incubation template with a fixed 2-week lag to hospitalization; useful as a baseline when waning immunity is not strongly expressed within the observed window.
